analysis.title: We warned about Taiwan. What comes next? (Goldman downgrades Taiwan)
key_insights: The Market Ear's late-October Taiwan warning has played out. It cited positioning at the 91st percentile of its five-year range and a divergence versus Korea and the semiconductor complex. Its preferred expression was the December EWT 95 put, which paid off.
Goldman cut Taiwan from Overweight to Market Weight and lowered its TAIEX target from 57,500 to 50,000, a 13% cut. The new end-2027 target still implies close to 20% upside.
Goldman forecasts EPS growth of 32% in 2027 and 25% in 2028. It also cut its target forward P/E to 14x, so the multiple, not earnings, is the constraint on returns.

Goldman expects Taiwan GDP growth to slow from 13% in 2026 to 6.3% in 2027. Tech's direct contribution falls from 9.3 to 4.8 percentage points, while tech's share of total growth rises from 72% to 77%.

Foreign investors sold about $89B of Taiwanese equities YTD, including $18.6B over the past month and $2.9B in the latest week. Domestic ETF inflows of about $80B and record brokerage cash of $148B absorb much of the selling.

Hedge-fund exposure to Taiwan is at the 85th percentile of the past five years. Asia ex-Japan active funds are 530bp underweight and global EM active funds are 425bp underweight. Taiwan Tech Hardware & Semis is the largest sector underweight. The underweights are possible fuel for a squeeze.
Goldman highlights record leveraged-ETF exposure and elevated margin balances in Taiwan. Leveraged ETF rebalancing and margin-related selling could amplify a selloff.
Taiwan is 27% of MSCI Asia Pacific ex-Japan, with about 85% AI-related exposure. Implied volatility is above 30%.
BofA data shows Taiwan's AI trade exposure relative to GDP is far above most regional peers.
The Market Ear says Taiwan is back at its long-term trendline and still below its 200-day moving average. It says the burden of proof remains with the bulls until Taiwan reclaims the 200-day.

tension_points.bull_case: Active managers are 530bp (Asia ex-Japan) and 425bp (global EM) underweight, and domestic liquidity (about $80B ETF inflows, $148B brokerage cash) keeps absorbing foreign selling. These underweights could fuel a squeeze. Goldman's end-2027 target still implies close to 20% upside.
tension_points.bear_case: Foreign investors have sold about $89B YTD, hedge-fund exposure is at the 85th percentile, leverage is at records, and the AI growth cycle is decelerating with a lower target P/E of 14x. The index is below its 200-day moving average.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Taiwan reclaiming its 200-day moving average would repair the technical damage and weaken the bear case. Staying below it raises the risk of another leg lower.

theme_stances.key_argument: Earnings growth stays strong, but the multiple is the problem and positioning and leverage leave the market vulnerable.
theme_stances.evidence: The multiple is becoming the problem.
